drivingQuestion: How should a person account for suffering that befalls him, and which afflictions are 'afflictions of love'?
outcomeNote: R' Yoḥanan's inclusive definition — both kinds are afflictions of love — stands: the verse that seemed to restrict it (ומתורתך תלמדנו) is re-read as teaching the worth of suffering a fortiori from the freeing of a slave for tooth or eye, and Resh Lakish's gezera shava on ברית is brought as the same conclusion.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ, כְּאִלּוּ אוֹחֵז חֶרֶב שֶׁל שְׁתֵּי פִיּוֹת בְּיָדוֹ. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״רוֹמְמוֹת אֵל בִּגְרוֹנָם וְחֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת בְּיָדָם״, מַאי מַשְׁמַע? אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: מֵרֵישָׁא דְעִנְיָנָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״יַעְלְזוּ חֲסִידִים בְּכָבוֹד יְרַנְּנוּ עַל מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָם״. וּכְתִיב בָּתְרֵיהּ: ״רוֹמְמוֹת אֵל בִּגְרוֹנָם וְחֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת בְּיָדָם״.
segments.en: The Gemara continues its treatment of the recitation of Shema upon one’s bed. «Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Anyone who recites Shema on his bed, it is as if he holds a double-edged sword,» guarding him from all evil, «as it is stated: “High praises of God in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands”» (Psalms 149:6). The Gemara asks: «From where is it inferred» that this verse from Psalms refers to the recitation of Shema? «Mar Zutra, and some say Rav Ashi, said:» We derive it «from the preceding» verse, «as it is written: “Let the pious exult in glory; let them joyously sing upon their beds.”» The praise of God from one’s bed is the recitation of Shema. «And it is written thereafter: “High praises of God in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands.”»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ — מַזִּיקִין בְּדֵילִין הֵימֶנּוּ. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְנֵי רֶשֶׁף יַגְבִּיהוּ עוּף״, וְאֵין ״עוּף״ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֲתָעִיף עֵינֶיךָ בּוֹ וְאֵינֶנּוּ״. וְאֵין ״רֶשֶׁף״ אֶלָּא מַזִּיקִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְזֵי רָעָב וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף וְקֶטֶב מְרִירִי״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Anyone who recites Shema upon his bed, demons stay away from him.» This is alluded to, «as it is stated:» “But man is born into trouble, «and the sparks [reshef ] fly [uf ] upward”» (Job 5:7). The verse is explained: The word «fly [uf ]» means «nothing other than Torah,» as Torah is difficult to grasp and easy to lose, like something that floats away, «as it is stated: “Will you set your eyes upon it? It is gone;» for riches certainly make themselves wings, like an eagle that flies into the heavens” (Proverbs 23:5). The word «“sparks”» means «nothing other than demons, as it is stated: “Wasting of hunger, and the devouring of the sparks [reshef] and bitter destruction [ketev meriri],» and the teeth of beasts I will send upon them, with the venom of crawling things of the dust” (Deuteronomy 32:24). Here we see reshef listed along with ketev meriri, both of which are understood by the Sages to be names of demons.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה — יִסּוּרִין בְּדֵילִין הֵימֶנּוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְנֵי רֶשֶׁף יַגְבִּיהוּ עוּף״. וְאֵין ״עוּף״ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הֲתָעִיף עֵינֶיךָ בּוֹ וְאֵינֶנּוּ״, וְאֵין ״רֶשֶׁף״ אֶלָּא יִסּוּרִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְזֵי רָעָב וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף״.
segments.en: Regarding this unclear verse, «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: If one engages in Torah» study, «suffering stays away from him, as it is stated: “And the sparks fly upward.”» And «fly» means «nothing other than Torah, «as it is stated: “Will you set your eyes upon it? It is gone;» and sparks» means «nothing other than suffering, as it is stated: “Wasting of hunger, and the devouring of the sparks,”» equating devouring sparks with wasting hunger, as both are types of suffering. From here, we derive that through Torah, fly, one is able to distance himself, upward, from suffering, sparks.

segments.he: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָא אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן, יוֹדְעִין אוֹתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹל ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו תַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֹתָיו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ כׇּל חֻקָּיו כׇּל הַמַּחֲלָה אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְמִצְרַיִם לֹא אָשִׂים עָלֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ רוֹפְאֶךָ״. אֶלָּא: כׇּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ עוֹסֵק — הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא עָלָיו יִסּוּרִין מְכוֹעָרִין וְעוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״נֶאֱלַמְתִּי דוּמִיָּה הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי מִטּוֹב וּכְאֵבִי נֶעְכָּר״, וְאֵין ״טוֹב״ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם תּוֹרָתִי אַל תַּעֲזֹבוּ״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: Even schoolchildren,» who learn only the Written Torah, «know this» concept «as it is stated: “And He said you shall surely hear the voice of the Lord your God, and what is upright in His eyes you shall do and you shall listen to His mitzvot and guard His statutes; any disease that I have placed upon Egypt I will not place upon you for I am the Lord your healer”» (Exodus 15:26). «Rather,» one must interpret the verse: «Anyone who is able to engage in Torah» study «yet does not engage» in that study, not only does «the Holy One, Blessed be He,» fail to protect him, but He «brings upon him hideous afflictions,» that embarrass him «and trouble him, as it is stated: “I was mute with silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was strong”» (Psalms 39:3). The word «good» means «nothing other than Torah, as it is stated: “For I have given you a good portion, My Torah, do not abandon it”» (Proverbs 4:2). The verse should be understood: “I have been silent from the study of Torah, and my pain was strong.”

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם. מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם, אָדָם מוֹכֵר חֵפֶץ לַחֲבֵירוֹ, מוֹכֵר עָצֵב, וְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂמֵחַ, אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵּן, נָתַן לָהֶם תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל — וְשָׂמַח, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם תּוֹרָתִי אַל תַּעֲזֹבוּ״.
segments.en: With regard to the verse: “For I have given you a good portion,” «Rabbi Zeira, and some say Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa, said: Come and see how the characteristics of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are unlike the characteristics of flesh and blood. It is characteristic of flesh and blood that when one sells an object to another» person, «the seller grieves» the loss of his possession «and the buyer rejoices. With regard to the Holy One, Blessed be He,» however, «this is not so. He gave the Torah to Israel and rejoiced, as it is stated: “For I have given you a good portion, My Torah, do not abandon it.”» A good portion is understood as a good purchase; although God sold Torah to Israel, He rejoices in the sale and praises the object before its new owner (Rabbi Yoshiyahu Pinto).

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב חִסְדָּא: אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁיִּסּוּרִין בָּאִין עָלָיו — יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״נַחְפְּשָׂה דְרָכֵינוּ וְנַחְקֹרָה וְנָשׁוּבָה עַד ה׳״. פִּשְׁפֵּשׁ וְלֹא מָצָא — יִתְלֶה בְּבִטּוּל תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר תְּיַסְּרֶנּוּ יָּהּ וּמִתּוֹרָתְךָ תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ״.
segments.en: Previously, the Gemara discussed suffering that results from one’s transgressions. The Gemara shifts the focus and discusses suffering that does not result from one’s transgressions and the suffering of the righteous. «Rava, and some say Rav Ḥisda, said: If a person sees that suffering has befallen him, he should examine his actions.» Generally, suffering comes about as punishment for one’s transgressions, «as it is stated: “We will search and examine our ways, and return to God”» (Lamentations 3:40). «If he examined» his ways and «found no» transgression for which that suffering is appropriate, «he may attribute» his suffering «to dereliction» in the study «of Torah.» God punishes an individual for dereliction in the study of Torah in order to emphasize the gravity of the issue, «as it is stated: “Happy is the man whom You punish, Lord, and teach out of Your law”» (Psalms 94:12). This verse teaches us that his suffering will cause him to return to Your law.

segments.he: וְאִם תָּלָה וְלֹא מָצָא — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁיִּסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה הֵם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.
segments.en: «And if he did attribute» his suffering to dereliction in the study of Torah, «and did not find» this to be so, «he may be confident that these are afflictions of love, as it is stated: “For whom the Lord loves, He rebukes,» as does a father the son in whom he delights” (Proverbs 3:12).

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָפַץ בּוֹ — מְדַכְּאוֹ בְּיִסּוּרִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַה׳ חָפֵץ דַּכְּאוֹ הֶחֱלִי״.
segments.en: So too, «Rava said» that «Rav Seḥora said» that «Rav Huna said: Anyone in whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights, He oppresses him with suffering, as it is stated: “Yet in whom the Lord delights, He oppresses him with disease;» to see if his soul would offer itself in guilt, that he might see his children, lengthen his days, and that the desire of the Lord might prosper by his hand” (Isaiah 53:10). This verse illustrates that in whomever God delights, he afflicts with illness.

segments.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ לֹא קִבְּלָם מֵאַהֲבָה? — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם תָּשִׂים אָשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹ״, מָה אָשָׁם לְדַעַת, אַף יִסּוּרִין — לְדַעַת.
segments.en: I «might» have thought that God delights in him even «if he does not accept» his suffering «with love. Therefore the verse teaches: “If his soul would offer itself in guilt.” Just as a guilt-offering is brought knowingly,» as it is one of the sacrifices offered willingly, without coercion, «so too» his «suffering» must be accepted «knowingly.»

segments.he: וְאִם קִבְּלָם מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ: ״יִרְאֶה זֶרַע יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים״. וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁתַּלְמוּדוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְחֵפֶץ ה׳ בְּיָדוֹ יִצְלָח״.
segments.en: «And if one accepts» that suffering with love, «what is his reward?» As the second part of the verse states: «“That he might see his children, lengthen his days.” Moreover,» in addition to these earthly rewards, «his» Torah «study will endure» and his Torah study will be successful, «as it is stated: “The purpose of the Lord,”» the Torah, the revelation of God’s will, «“might prosper by his hand.”»

segments.he: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי וְרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא. חַד אָמַר: אֵלּוּ הֵם יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה — כׇּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן בִּטּוּל תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר תְּיַסְּרֶנּוּ יָּהּ וּמִתּוֹרָתְךָ תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ״.
segments.en: With regard to the acceptance of affliction with love and what exactly this entails, «Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi and Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina disagree. One» of them «said: Afflictions of love are any that do not cause dereliction» in the study «of Torah,» i.e., any which do not afflict his body to the extent that he is unable to study Torah, «as it is stated: “Happy is the man whom You afflict, Lord, and teach from Your Torah.”» Afflictions of love are when You “teach from Your Torah.”

segments.he: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵלּוּ הֵן יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה — כׇּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן בִּטּוּל תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בָּרוּךְ אֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא הֵסִיר תְּפִלָּתִי וְחַסְדּוֹ מֵאִתִּי״.
segments.en: «And one said: Afflictions of love are any that do not cause dereliction» in the recitation «of prayer, as it is stated: “Blessed is God Who did not turn away my prayer”» (Psalms 66:20). Despite his suffering, the afflicted is still capable of praying to God.

segments.he: אָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה הֵן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said:» My father, «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said as follows: Both,» even afflictions that cause dereliction in the study of Torah and those that cause dereliction in the recitation of prayer, «are afflictions of love,» as with regard to one who suffers without transgression «it is stated: “For whom He loves, He rebukes,”» and inability to study Torah and to pray are among his afflictions.

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וּמִתּוֹרָתְךָ תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ״ — אַל תִּקְרֵי ״תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ״, אֶלָּא תְלַמְּדֵנוּ. דָּבָר זֶה — מִתּוֹרָתְךָ תְּלַמְּדֵנוּ.
segments.en: «What then,» is the meaning when «the verse states: “And teach him from Your Torah”? Do not read and teach» to mean and «teach him», «rather, and teach us». «You teach us» the value of «this» affliction «from Your Torah.»

segments.he: קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִשֵּׁן וָעַיִן. מַה שֵּׁן וָעַיִן שֶׁהֵן אֶחָד מֵאֵבָרָיו שֶׁל אָדָם — עֶבֶד יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן לְחֵרוּת, יִסּוּרִין שֶׁמְּמָרְקִין כׇּל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם — עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
segments.en: This is taught through «an a fortiori inference from» the law concerning «the tooth and eye» of a slave: «The tooth and eye are» each «a single limb of a person» and if his master damages either, «the slave thereby obtains his freedom; suffering that cleanses a person’s entire body all the more so» that one attains freedom, atonement, from his sins.

segments.he: וְהַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: נֶאֱמַר ״בְּרִית״ בְּמֶלַח, וְנֶאֱמַר ״בְּרִית״ בְּיִסּוּרִין, נֶאֱמַר ״בְּרִית״ בְּמֶלַח, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְלֹא תַשְׁבִּית מֶלַח בְּרִית״ וְנֶאֱמַר ״בְּרִית״ בְּיִסּוּרִין, דִּכְתִיב: ״אֵלֶּה דִבְרֵי הַבְּרִית״, מַה ״בְּרִית״ הָאָמוּר בְּמֶלַח — מֶלַח מְמַתֶּקֶת אֶת הַבָּשָׂר, אַף ״בְּרִית״ הָאָמוּר בְּיִסּוּרִין — יִסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם.
segments.en: «And that is» the statement of «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:» The word «covenant is used with regard to salt, and» the word «covenant is used with regard to afflictions.» The word «covenant is used with regard to salt, as it is written: “The salt of the covenant» with your God «should not be excluded» from your meal-offering; with all your sacrifices you must offer salt” (Leviticus 2:13). «And» the word «covenant is used with regard to afflictions, as it is written: “These are the words of the covenant”» (Deuteronomy 28:69). «Just as,» in «the covenant mentioned with regard to salt, the salt sweetens» the taste of «the meat» and renders it edible, «so too» in «the covenant mentioned with regard to suffering, the suffering cleanses a person’s transgressions,» purifying him for a more sublime existence.

moves.summary: Reciting Shema on one's bed is like holding a double-edged sword.
moves.about: prooftext that reciting Shema on one's bed is like holding a double-edged sword

moves.summary: The Gemara asks what in that verse indicates the recitation of Shema.
moves.about: on what basis Psalms 149:6 indicates the recitation of Shema at all

moves.cueHe: אמר מר זוטרא ואיתימא רב אשי
moves.summary: Mar Zutra (or Rav Ashi) answers: from the opening of the passage.
moves.about: the verse's reference to Shema is fixed by the preceding verse about singing on one's bed

moves.summary: Psalms 149:6, 'a double-edged sword in their hands', is brought as the prooftext.
moves.about: an alternative attribution of the derivation מרישא דעניינא, reported alongside Mar Zutra without deciding

moves.summary: The preceding verse, 'let them sing upon their beds', and then its sequel, are cited to fix the reference.
moves.about: the preceding verse, whose 'sing upon their beds' is read as the recitation of Shema

moves.summary: A second dictum of R' Yitzḥak: demons keep away from one who recites Shema on his bed.
moves.about: prooftext that demons keep away from one who recites Shema on his bed

moves.summary: עוף is glossed as Torah and רשף as demons, each with its own supporting verse.
moves.about: prooftext that עוף denotes Torah

moves.summary: Job 5:7, 'and the sparks fly upward', is brought as the prooftext.
moves.about: glossing עוף as Torah and רשף as demons, so the verse says Torah drives demons away

moves.summary: Resh Lakish expounds the same obscure verse the other way: רשף is suffering, kept away by Torah study.
moves.about: prooftext that suffering keeps away from one who engages in Torah

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי יוחנן: הא אפילו תינוקות של בית רבן יודעין אותו
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan tells him the teaching is superfluous — even schoolchildren know it.
moves.about: that Resh Lakish's derivation teaches nothing, since even schoolchildren know from an explicit verse that obedience averts affliction

moves.summary: Psalms 39:3 is expounded with טוב glossed as Torah from Proverbs 4:2.
moves.about: prooftext that silence from Torah brings strong pain

moves.summary: Exodus 15:26 is cited as the explicit verse schoolchildren already know.
moves.about: the explicit verse schoolchildren already know, brought to show Resh Lakish's teaching adds nothing

moves.summary: Instead: one who could study Torah and does not has hideous afflictions brought upon him.
moves.about: the non-obvious teaching to put in place of Resh Lakish's — that one who could study Torah and does not has hideous afflictions brought upon him

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי זירא ואיתימא רבי חנינא בר פפא
moves.summary: On the same verse 'a good portion I have given you': unlike a human seller, God rejoiced when He gave Israel the Torah.
moves.about: prooftext that God gave the Torah and rejoiced, unlike a human seller

moves.summary: One who sees suffering come upon him should examine his deeds.
moves.about: prooftext that one should search his ways when suffering comes

moves.summary: If he found no transgression, he may attribute the suffering to neglect of Torah, per Psalms 94:12.
moves.about: an alternative attribution of the ruling that one who sees suffering should examine his deeds

moves.summary: Lamentations 3:40, 'we will search our ways', is the prooftext.
moves.about: prooftext that unexplained suffering may be attributed to dereliction in Torah study

moves.summary: If that too yields nothing, these are known to be afflictions of love, per Proverbs 3:12.
moves.about: prooftext that suffering left unexplained is known to be affliction of love

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא, אמר רב סחורה, אמר רב הונא
moves.summary: Transmitted through Rava and Rav Seḥora: whomever God delights in He crushes with suffering.
moves.about: prooftext that God crushes with illness the one He delights in

moves.summary: Isaiah 53:10, 'the Lord delighted to crush him with disease', is the prooftext.
moves.about: the teaching that God crushes with suffering whomever He delights in

moves.summary: One might have floated that God delights in him even if he did not accept the suffering with love.
moves.about: excluding the floated reading that God delights in the sufferer even when he does not accept the suffering with love

moves.summary: The continuation of the verse, 'if his soul would offer itself in guilt', excludes that floated reading.
moves.about: comparing suffering to a guilt-offering: as the offering is brought knowingly, suffering must be accepted knowingly

moves.summary: As a guilt-offering is brought knowingly, so suffering must be accepted knowingly.
The reward for accepting: offspring, long life, and Torah study that endures.
moves.about: the remainder of the same verse, adduced for the reward of one who accepts suffering with love

moves.actor: unnamed:חד אמר — יסורין שאין בהן ביטול תורה
moves.cueHe: פליגי בה רבי יעקב בר אידי ורבי אחא בר חנינא. חד אמר
moves.summary: A dispute over what afflictions of love are: one holds they are those that do not prevent Torah study.
moves.about: prooftext that afflictions of love leave one able to study Torah

moves.actor: unnamed:חד אמר — יסורין שאין בהן ביטול תורה
moves.summary: Psalms 94:12, 'and teach him from Your Torah', is his prooftext.

moves.actor: unnamed:חד אמר — יסורין שאין בהן ביטול תפלה
moves.summary: The other holds they are those that do not prevent prayer.
moves.about: prooftext that afflictions of love leave one able to pray

moves.actor: unnamed:חד אמר — יסורין שאין בהן ביטול תפלה
moves.summary: Psalms 66:20, 'who did not turn away my prayer', is his prooftext.

moves.actor: ר׳ אבא בריה דר׳ חייא בר אבא
moves.cueHe: אמר להו רבי אבא בריה דרבי חייא בר אבא, הכי אמר רבי חייא בר אבא, אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: He reports his father's version of R' Yoḥanan: both kinds alike are afflictions of love.
moves.about: his father's version of R' Yoḥanan's ruling that both kinds are afflictions of love

moves.summary: Proverbs 3:12, 'for whom He loves, He rebukes', is the prooftext for the inclusive definition.
moves.about: prooftext that all suffering of one without transgression is rebuke out of love

moves.summary: If both kinds count, what does the clause 'and teach him from Your Torah' still teach?
moves.about: what the clause ומתורתך תלמדנו teaches once both kinds of affliction are afflictions of love, so that the clause no longer restricts them

moves.summary: Read 'teach us' rather than 'teach him': the worth of suffering is what Torah teaches us.
moves.about: re-vocalising תלמדנו as 'teach us', so the clause says the value of suffering is learned from the Torah

moves.summary: The Torah teaches it a fortiori: if a slave goes free for a single limb, suffering that scours the whole body all the more so.
moves.about: the a fortiori the verse licenses: if a slave goes free for one limb, suffering that scours the whole body all the more so brings release

moves.summary: The Gemara identifies this conclusion with Resh Lakish's teaching.
moves.about: Resh Lakish's gezera shava on ברית, brought as the same idea the a fortiori reached

moves.cueHe: דאמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: נאמר ״ברית״ במלח
moves.summary: A gezera shava on ברית: as salt sweetens meat, afflictions scour all a person's transgressions.
moves.about: the occurrence of ברית with regard to salt, one leg of the gezera shava
